key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant, because defect-assisted recombination is strongly suppressed even when deep gap states are present.
engineering_relevance: This makes t-Se a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where low recombination can help preserve voltage and efficiency.
method: First-principles calculations of point defects in trigonal selenium
Shockley-Read-Hall recombination analysis for both radiative and nonradiative pathways
Survey of a large, chemically diverse defect set across defect levels, charge states, and doping conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that nonradiative capture is suppressed by large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per recombination event, and that realistic defect concentrations cannot explain the observed efficiency losses.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on computed defect physics, so device behavior may still depend on growth quality, defect populations, and other loss mechanisms beyond point defects.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
